findings.reason: without a clause saying the derived log must itself record the verdict in the shape promotion reads (a terminal `EXIT=` record), the node implements exactly the derivation the section names and the first case still refuses, costing a repair round.
findings.text: §1's deliverable says promotion "derives the verdict and the log from" the stored review record, but at this head a promotion that does that is refused: `tests/test_a_review_runs_promotion_derives_its_own_gate.py::test_case1_no_gate_flags_with_a_json_list_tests_field` fails with "its cited log … carries no terminal EXIT=<n> line … a log without one states no status at all" (`reckon/crew/promotion_checks.py` / `reckon/crew/promotion_evidence.py:1659`), so a record-derived log can never satisfy the promotion it exists to carry

findings.reason: naming the existing test file and requiring its four cases to pass at the head (rather than only a clean delta) is what makes the gate able to fail, and this is the same shape as §12/§21's answer.
findings.text: the done-when's only delta is "the test files importing the modules changed add no failure against a base arm", but the four cases it lists are already written at main in `tests/test_a_review_runs_promotion_derives_its_own_gate.py` and three of them fail at this head, so a node measuring the delta records zero added failures while the deliverable's own cases stay red

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `reckon/crew/promotion_checks.py`, `reckon/crew/recovery_review_delivery.py`, `crew check --review`, `crew complete --run <id>` and `--gate` all resolve at this head, and §10 is the section that owns the `tests:` field's shape.
